page: Vultr voc-c-1c-2gb-25s-amd is an entry-level instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 1 physical core and 1 thread running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory and 25 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, alongside a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core execution and memory-intensive or multi-threaded operations. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the instance achieves a score of 3373.08, placing it in the top 10% tier. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also perform strongly, with gzip compression reaching 31.6 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.2 GB/sec. However, due to the single-core constraint, multi-core stress-ng performance matches the single-core score, falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers.

Memory performance is generally limited on this hardware profile. Read-only bandwidth testing falls in the bottom 25%, registering 165.89 GB/sec for small blocks and 35.29 GB/sec for large blocks, though write bandwidth for large blocks maintains an average tier at 32.48 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the bottom 25%, reflecting these memory and concurrency limitations.

The primary trade-off of this instance lies in its resource density. While the dedicated AMD EPYC core delivers strong single-threaded compute capabilities, the 2.0 GB memory capacity and low memory bandwidth constrain its utility for memory-heavy or highly concurrent workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a low-cost entry point to dedicated CPU resources, making it suitable for workloads that require predictable CPU allocation without the overhead of multi-core scaling. This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic utility scripting, simple web serving with low concurrency, and small-scale development or testing environments.
